[
  "When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1-3mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis.",
  "Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and on the genitalia.",
  "The consensus rate for this recommendation is 100% (21/21).",
  "Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first-line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness, as well as for melanoma in situ.",
  "Surgical margins should be based on tumor thickness.",
  "Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor, and in the same operative setting whenever possible.",
  "The criteria driving the 4-point score are pigment_network (atypical, 2 points), dots_and_globules (irregular, 1 point), and regression_structures (blue areas, 1 point).",
  "These features are major or minor features that contribute to melanoma suspicion.",
  "On the image, one should look for an atypical pigment network (irregular meshes and thickened lines).",
  "One should look for irregularly distributed dots or globules.",
  "One should look for blue areas indicating regression structures.",
  "These features are sufficient to trigger the 7-point checklist’s threshold and warrant management aligned with melanoma suspicion."
]
